text: You're learning to talk. {mother} and {father} lean in, waiting for your first word.

choices.label: Say "Mama"
choices.outcome: Your first word was "Mama". {mother} cried a little.

choices.label: Say "Dada"
choices.outcome: Your first word was "Dada". {father} told everyone.

choices.label: Say "No"
choices.outcome: Your first word was "No". It set the tone.

text: You found the crayons. The living-room wall looks very empty.

choices.label: Draw a masterpiece
choices.outcome: You drew a sun with a face on the wall. {father} took a photo before scrubbing it off.

choices.label: Draw on paper instead
choices.outcome: You drew on paper like a tiny professional.

choices.label: Eat a crayon
choices.outcome: You ate the blue one. No regrets.

text: {sibling} grabbed your favourite toy and won't give it back.

choices.label: Bite him
choices.outcome: You bit {sibling}. You both got sent to your rooms.

choices.label: Tell {mother}
choices.outcome: {mother} made {sibling} give it back. He sulked all day.

choices.label: Let him have it
choices.outcome: You let {sibling} keep it. He shared his biscuits later.

text: Your first day of school. A boy in a dinosaur jumper is crying by the gate.

choices.label: Hold his hand
choices.outcome: You held his hand. His name is Tomás, and he is now your best friend.

choices.label: Run to the swings
choices.outcome: You ran straight to the swings and claimed them.

choices.label: Cry too
choices.outcome: You cried too. Solidarity.

text: It's show-and-tell. Everyone else brought a pet or a trophy.

choices.label: Bring a rock
choices.outcome: You gave a passionate talk about a rock. The teacher loved it.

choices.label: Bring {father}'s phone
choices.outcome: You showed the class {father}'s photos. Some were embarrassing.

choices.label: Pretend you forgot
choices.outcome: You said you forgot. Nobody noticed.

text: Tomás invites you to his birthday. The same day, the coolest kid in class has a party too.

choices.label: Go to Tomás's party
choices.outcome: You went to Tomás's party. He didn't stop smiling.

choices.label: Go to the cool party
choices.outcome: The cool party was fun. Tomás saw the photos.

text: Big maths test tomorrow. You haven't opened the book.

choices.label: Study all night
choices.outcome: You studied all night and passed with a good mark.

choices.label: Copy from your neighbour
choices.outcome: You copied answers. You passed, barely.

choices.label: Wing it
choices.outcome: You winged it. The result is not going on the fridge.

text: A kid called Duarte keeps knocking your books out of your hands in the corridor.

choices.label: Stand up to him
choices.outcome: You told Duarte to stop, loudly, in front of everyone. He did.

choices.label: Tell a teacher
choices.outcome: You told a teacher. Duarte got detention and a reputation.

choices.label: Take another route
choices.outcome: You took the long way round for the rest of the year.

text: You've been begging for a pet for months. {mother} finally sighs: "Fine. One."

choices.label: A dog
choices.outcome: You named the dog Biscoito. He chewed everything you owned.

choices.label: A cat
choices.outcome: The cat chose you. Then ignored you. Perfect.

choices.label: A goldfish
choices.outcome: The goldfish lived for eleven glorious days.

text: Biscoito is old now. The vet says it's time.

choices.label: Be there with him
choices.outcome: You held Biscoito until the end. It was the right thing.

choices.label: Let your parents go
choices.outcome: You couldn't face it. {mother} told you he went peacefully.

text: Secondary school is all about groups. Three of them have noticed you.

choices.label: The drama kids
choices.outcome: You joined the drama kids. You learned to cry on cue.

choices.label: The athletes
choices.outcome: You joined the athletes. Training at 7 a.m. became your life.

choices.label: The coders
choices.outcome: You joined the coding club and built a terrible game.

text: Time to pick an elective for next year.

choices.label: Cooking
choices.outcome: You chose cooking. Your first omelette was a crime scene, the second was art.

choices.label: Music
choices.outcome: You chose music and fell for the drums. Your family did not.

choices.label: Economics
choices.outcome: You chose economics and started reading the business news.

text: You can't stop thinking about someone in your class. They just smiled at you.

choices.label: Write them a note
choices.outcome: You wrote a note. They wrote back "maybe". It was the best day of the year.

choices.label: Tell your friends
choices.outcome: You told your friends. By lunch, the whole school knew.

choices.label: Keep it secret
choices.outcome: You kept it secret. Some things are just for you.

text: There's a party at a friend's house. Their parents are away. {mother} thinks you're at the library.

choices.label: Go to the party
choices.outcome: You went. It was loud, messy and unforgettable.

choices.label: Actually go to the library
choices.outcome: You went to the library. Your grades thanked you.

choices.label: Ask {mother} for permission
choices.outcome: {mother} said yes, if you're home by eleven. You were.

text: {mother} found the photos from that party. She knows you weren't at the library.

choices.label: Apologise
choices.outcome: You apologised properly. It took a while, but she forgave you.

choices.label: Argue back
choices.outcome: You argued. Doors were slammed. Nobody won.

text: Driving test day. The examiner has a clipboard and no sense of humour.

choices.label: Drive carefully
choices.outcome: You passed first time.

choices.label: Show off a bit
choices.outcome: You failed for "unnecessary confidence".

text: School is over. What's next?

choices.label: Go to university
choices.outcome: You enrolled at university in {city}.

choices.label: Start working
choices.outcome: You decided to start working straight away.

choices.label: Take a gap year
choices.outcome: You took a gap year and travelled with a backpack and no plan.

text: You need to choose your major.

choices.label: Culinary arts
choices.outcome: You chose culinary arts. Your flatmates ate very well.

choices.label: Law
choices.outcome: You chose law. The reading list is enormous.

choices.label: Computer science
choices.outcome: You chose computer science and discovered coffee.

text: Graduation day. {mother} brought a sign with your name on it. It is very large.

choices.label: Wave at {mother}
choices.outcome: You graduated and waved at {mother} from the stage.

choices.label: Pretend you don't know her
choices.outcome: You graduated. You pretended not to see the sign. She noticed.

text: Duarte, the kid who knocked your books over at school, is serving you coffee. He recognises you.

choices.label: Be kind
choices.outcome: You chatted. He apologised for school. You tipped well.

choices.label: Remind him
choices.outcome: You reminded him. He went red and gave you a free pastry.

text: Tomás is getting married. He asks you to be his best person: "You were there on day one."

choices.label: Say yes
choices.outcome: You gave a speech about a boy in a dinosaur jumper. Nobody had dry eyes.

choices.label: Say you're too busy
choices.outcome: You said you were too busy. He understood. Mostly.

text: You bump into Tomás in town. He's polite, but cold. He still remembers his birthday.

choices.label: Apologise, finally
choices.outcome: You apologised, years late. He laughed. "We were eight." You got coffee.

choices.label: Keep walking
choices.outcome: You nodded and kept walking.

text: A job interview is going well, until they ask about the shoplifting incident.

choices.label: Tell the truth
choices.outcome: You told the truth. They appreciated it, and offered you a trial shift.

choices.label: Deny it
choices.outcome: You denied it. They had the record. The interview ended there.

text: You found your first flat. It's tiny, and the shower has opinions.

choices.label: Take it
choices.outcome: You moved into your first flat. You ate cereal for dinner and loved it.

choices.label: Stay at home a bit longer
choices.outcome: You stayed home and saved money. {mother} kept doing your laundry.

text: Your grandmother left the family flat in {city} to you and {sibling}. He wants to sell it now. You don't.

choices.label: Sue him for it
choices.outcome: You took {sibling} to court and won the flat. He stopped answering your calls.

npcMemory.sibling: You sued me for Gran's flat.

choices.label: Sell and split it
choices.outcome: You sold the flat and split the money. Nobody was thrilled, but nobody was hurt.

choices.label: Give him your share
choices.outcome: You signed your half over to {sibling}. He hugged you for the first time in years.

text: {sibling}, the brother you sued over the flat, is at your door. He is holding a baby.

choices.label: Let him in
choices.outcome: You let him in. He said, "She's called Rosa. I wanted her to know her family." You both cried.

choices.label: Talk at the door
choices.outcome: You talked at the door. It was stiff, but it was a start.

choices.label: Close the door
choices.outcome: You closed the door. Later you saw the stroller tracks in the rain.

text: {sibling} turned Gran's flat into a little bakery. He wants to name a bread after you.

choices.label: Accept the honour
choices.outcome: There is now a sourdough named after you. It sells out daily.

choices.label: Ask for free bread instead
choices.outcome: You negotiated lifetime free bread. A wise deal.

text: A small restaurant in {city} needs a cook. The pay is bad. The kitchen smells amazing.

choices.label: Take the job
choices.outcome: You started as a line cook. Your hands burn and your heart sings.

choices.label: Keep it a hobby
choices.outcome: You kept cooking as a hobby. Your friends are grateful.

text: You've saved a little and there's an empty shop on your street. A restaurant of your own?

choices.label: Go for it
choices.outcome: You opened your own restaurant. Your name is on the door.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.outcome: You decided to wait. The shop became a phone repair store.

text: A friend pitches you a start-up idea: an app for sharing leftovers with neighbours.

choices.label: Invest your savings
choices.outcome: You invested. The app was clever, and so were the competitors.

choices.label: Pass
choices.outcome: You passed. You'll never know.

text: News about LeftOver, the start-up you invested in, is everywhere this morning.

choices.label: Open the news
choices.outcome: LeftOver was bought by a supermarket chain. Your share came to $22,000.

text: You've been exhausted for weeks. A friend says you look grey.

choices.label: See a doctor
choices.outcome: You saw a doctor. Low iron. A month of supplements and you felt human again.

choices.label: Push through
choices.outcome: You pushed through. It got worse before it got better.

text: It's {father}'s birthday this weekend.

choices.label: Cook him dinner
choices.outcome: You cooked {father}'s favourite. He had seconds and thirds.

choices.label: Send a message
choices.outcome: You sent a message with three emojis. He replied "thank you" with a full stop.

text: Someone called Amara laughs at your joke in a queue. A real laugh.

choices.label: Ask for her number
choices.outcome: You asked for Amara's number. She wrote it on your hand.

choices.label: Smile and leave
choices.outcome: You smiled and left. You thought about it all week.

text: Amara asks if you want to move in together.

choices.label: Yes
choices.outcome: You moved in with Amara. You argue about dishes. You're very happy.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.outcome: You said not yet. She said she understood. She went quiet for a week.

text: You've found a ring. Amara has no idea.

choices.label: Propose at dinner
choices.outcome: You proposed over dinner. She said yes before you finished the question.

choices.label: Wait for the perfect moment
choices.outcome: You decided to wait for the perfect moment. The ring is in your sock drawer.

text: You find a wallet on the pavement with $300 in it.

choices.label: Hand it in
choices.outcome: You handed it in. The owner sent a thank-you card.

choices.label: Keep the cash
choices.outcome: You kept the cash and binned the wallet.
